title: Epochal latency derivative alerting and trace anchors
creator: Sana Gupta
description:
Problem: Current SLO alerting at Redwood relies heavily on static burn-rate and threshold-based rules that either fire too early for spiky workloads or too late for slowly rising latency trends. On-call noise has increased for certain multi-tenant routes where transient upstream pressure looks identical to a sustained degradation. We also lack a tight mapping from alerts to the trace data that would allow first responders to rapidly identify root cause.

Proposal: Implement a two-part system: 1) epochal latency derivative alerts — detect changes in the time-derivative (rate of change) of percentile latencies across configurable epochs (e.g., 1m, 5m, 30m) and fire alerts when derivative exceeds adaptive thresholds that consider historical seasonality; and 2) trace anchors — when an alert fires, automatically attach a deterministic set of representative traces and span-anchored summaries (error stamps, top DB spans, top downstream hosts) to the alert payload so engineers have contextual anchors in the pager.

Goals: reduce noisy pages by 25% on routes with high transient variance, reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) by 40% for latency incidents, and improve first-touch diagnosis time by surfacing 3 representative traces per alert with summary metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Derivative alert rule type implemented in alerting service and configurable via Console rules UI
Alerting service computes and persists epochal derivative metrics for p50/p95/p99 and exposes them to rules engine
Default adaptive thresholds available and tunable per-route; historical seasonality window configurable
Trace anchors are attached to each fired alert: up to 3 representative traces plus automated span_summary (top 5 spans by time and top error types)
Integration tests covering spike + gradual-deg scenarios that validate alert firing and suppression behavior
On-call runbook updated with guidance for derivative alerts and how to use trace anchors for triage
Metric showing noise reduction (pages per route) available in Console within 1 week of rollout
implementation_steps: Add epochal derivative aggregator in metrics pipeline (Prometheus/TSDB consumer) to produce derivative series for p50/p95/p99
Extend rules engine schema to accept 'derivative' rule type with epoch window, smoothing, and adaptive-threshold params
Implement adaptive threshold estimator service using rolling quantiles and seasonality correction following the design doc
Instrument alert payload to request 3 representative traces from tracing service and attach span_summary manifest
Console: add UI for creating derivative-based alerts and previewing attached trace anchors
Backfill and shadow mode: run rules in shadow for 48 hours on a fraction of traffic before enabling pages
Execute staged rollout: alpha tenants -> beta -> org-wide with monitoring of noise and MTTA metrics
rollout_plan: Week 0: Integration tests and internal alpha with Canary team on dev cluster
Week 1: Shadow mode for top 20 high-variance routes (no pages) and collect signal for thresholds
Week 2: Enable paging for beta tenants with doubled snooze window and extra oncall coverage
Week 3: Full rollout with default conservative thresholds and telemetry dashboards enabled
Post-rollout: 4-week watch with daily reviews and threshold tuning; optionally rollback if pages increase
test_plan: Unit tests for derivative aggregator and rules engine predicates
E2E tests simulating sudden spikes, slow-rises, and recovery patterns to assert correct firing/suppression
Load test to ensure derivative computation adds <5% CPU to metrics ingestion pipeline at peak
Chaos test: introduce downstream latency in staging and verify trace anchors correctly surface top spans
Observability: dashboards for pages-by-route, MTTA, MTTR, and representative-trace-attached ratio
risks: False positives if seasonality estimator mis-calibrates; mitigated by shadow mode and conservative defaults
Increased load on tracing service retrieving representative traces per alert; mitigate with cache TTL and lightweight span_summary extraction
UI complexity: too many knobs could confuse PMs — provide templates and sane defaults
Cross-tenant privacy: need to ensure trace anchors do not leak sensitive PII across org boundaries
